config.title: Props Drilling

intro.title: Props Drilling
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React app with TypeScript to understand props drilling. You will create a family of nested components that pass data from a parent component down through multiple levels of child components using props. The core concept is learning how to manage and pass data through a component hierarchy without using state management libraries. You will work with React functional components, TypeScript interfaces for type-safe props, and JSX for rendering. This hands-on exercise will show you the basics of component communication and the challenges of passing props through many layers.
intro.usecase: Props drilling is a common pattern in React applications where data must be passed through multiple intermediate components to reach a deeply nested child. You'll encounter this when building complex UIs like e-commerce dashboards, where a user's filter selection (e.g., price range) needs to travel from a top-level toolbar down to individual product cards. Similarly, in multi-step forms or settings panels, user input often needs to be passed through several layout components before reaching the final submission handler. While straightforward for shallow hierarchies, managing this flow across many levels highlights the need for more scalable state solutions.

objectives: Construct a React component hierarchy with three levels of nesting
Initialize and pass primitive data types as props through multiple component levels
Manipulate and update prop values at intermediate component levels without direct usage
Configure TypeScript interfaces to define and enforce prop types across the component chain
Integrate callback functions as props to enable data flow back up the component hierarchy
Render components that display prop values received through multiple layers of drilling
Apply props drilling patterns to share user authentication state through a component tree

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and useState from 'react' at the top of your file.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in the necessary modules for React development.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing modules
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The file will have the required imports to use React and the useState hook.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to import React and useState from 'react' to proceed.

steps.title: Create the main App component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns null for now. Use TypeScript by adding the appropriate type annotation.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax. Remember to specify the return type as JSX.Element or React.ReactElement.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the App component here
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is defined with proper TypeScript typing and returns null.
successCriteria: App component is created with correct TypeScript annotation and returns null
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created the App component, but check if you included the TypeScript return type annotation.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component wasn't created correctly. Make sure to define a functional component named App that returns null with proper TypeScript typing.

steps.title: Initialize user state in App
steps.instruction: Inside the App component, initialize a user state with name and age using useState. The state should be an object with properties name (string) and age (number).
steps.hint: Use useState with an initial value like { name: '', age: 0 } and destructure the state variable and setter function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: state initialization for user data
const [user, setUser] = useState({ name: 'John', age: 25 });
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will have a user state variable and setUser function ready to pass down to child components via props drilling.
successCriteria: user state is initialized with useState, containing name (string) and age (number) properties
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've initialized state, but make sure it's an object with both name (string) and age (number) properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The user state needs to be initialized with useState, containing both name and age properties. Try using: const [user, setUser] = useState({ name: '', age: 0 });

steps.title: Create the UserProfile component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named UserProfile that will receive props. Define it with an empty body that returns null for now.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or an arrow function. Remember to name it exactly 'UserProfile'.
steps.expectedOutcome: A UserProfile component is defined and ready to receive props in the next step.
successCriteria: The code contains a functional component named UserProfile that returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined a component named UserProfile that returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The UserProfile component isn't defined correctly. Check that you've created a functional component with the exact name 'UserProfile' that returns null.

steps.title: Define props interface for UserProfile
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript interface named 'UserProfileProps' for the UserProfile component's props. It should have two properties: 'name' of type string and 'age' of type number.
steps.hint: Create an interface using the 'interface' keyword, then list the required properties with their types.
steps.expectedOutcome: An interface named UserProfileProps is defined with name: string and age: number properties.
successCriteria: The UserProfileProps interface is correctly defined with the required properties and types.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that your interface has both 'name' (string) and 'age' (number) properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface definition is missing or incorrect. Make sure to use the 'interface' keyword and include both required properties with correct types.

steps.title: Add UserProfile to App's JSX
steps.instruction: In the App component's return statement, render the UserProfile component and pass the user state as props.
steps.hint: Use JSX syntax to include the UserProfile component and pass the user state object as a prop.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component returns JSX that includes the UserProfile component with the user state passed as props.
successCriteria: UserProfile component is rendered in App's return statement with user state passed as props
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're passing the user state as a prop to UserProfile.
steps.feedbackWrong: The UserProfile component should be rendered in App's return statement with the user state passed as props.

steps.title: Create the UserDetails component
steps.instruction: Create a new functional component named UserDetails. It should be defined as a separate component after the UserProfile component.
steps.hint: Define a new component using either a function declaration or arrow function. You can start with a simple return statement like return null; for now.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new UserDetails component is defined in the code.
successCriteria: The UserDetails component is created as a functional component.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started creating the component, but make sure it's a functional component named UserDetails.
steps.feedbackWrong: The UserDetails component hasn't been created yet. Create a functional component named UserDetails.

steps.title: Add UserDetails to UserProfile
steps.instruction: Inside the UserProfile component, render the UserDetails component and pass the user prop through to it.
steps.hint: You'll need to add UserDetails as a JSX element inside UserProfile's return statement, and pass the user prop as a prop to UserDetails.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UserProfile component will render UserDetails and pass the user data through props, demonstrating props drilling through an intermediate component.
successCriteria: UserDetails is rendered inside UserProfile's JSX
The user prop is passed from UserProfile to UserDetails
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're rendering UserDetails inside UserProfile and passing the user prop to it.
steps.feedbackWrong: Inside UserProfile, you need to render the UserDetails component and pass the user prop to it.

steps.title: Display user data in UserDetails
steps.instruction: In the UserDetails component, display the user's name and email from the props in the existing JSX.
steps.hint: The props are already destructured as { user }. Use the user object's properties in the JSX.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UserDetails component should display the user's name and email from the props in the JSX.
successCriteria: UserDetails component renders the user's name and email from the props.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're accessing the user object's properties (name and email) in the JSX.
steps.feedbackWrong: The user data isn't displayed correctly. Check that you're using the user prop in the JSX.

steps.title: Create update handler in App
steps.instruction: Inside the App component, create a function named handleUpdateUser that takes a new user object and updates the user state using setUser.
steps.hint: The function should accept a parameter with the same type as the user state, then call setUser with that parameter.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component now has a handleUpdateUser function that can update the user state.
successCriteria: A function named handleUpdateUser is defined inside App that accepts a user object parameter and calls setUser with it.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it accepts a user parameter and calls setUser with it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleUpdateUser function should be defined inside App with proper parameter typing and setUser call.

steps.title: Add update button and wire handler
steps.instruction: Inside the App component's return statement, add a button element with an onClick handler that calls handleUpdateUser. The button text should be 'Update User'.
steps.hint: Add the button JSX element inside the return statement, before or after the UserProfile component.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button with click handler
<button onClick={handleClick}>Click Me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component now includes a button that, when clicked, updates the user state from John to Jane, demonstrating props drilling with handler passing.
successCriteria: A button element with onClick={handleUpdateUser} and text 'Update User' is added to the App component's return statement.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but it might be missing the onClick handler or the correct text. Make sure the button has onClick={handleUpdateUser} and displays 'Update User'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button element is not correctly added or wired. Check that you've added a button with onClick={handleUpdateUser} inside the App component's return statement.
